sarah_cust: Hey team — customer hitting truncated JSON when using streaming JSON mode. Payload ends mid-object, e.g. last bytes are '"content":"...\n"choices":[{' and then connection closes. Happening ~15% of streams since 2026-03-15. Request id r-9a7c2f. Can we triage?
support_elaine: sorry about that — can you paste the curl or client code you used and the request id(s)? Also which endpoint (chat/stream vs completions) and whether it's SSE or raw chunked stream?
sarah_cust: SSE endpoint /v1/chat/stream, here's a sanitized curl we used:
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rw-chat-ow-1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"generate json\nmode: structured"}],"stream":true}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/stream
```
It yields a lot of SSE events but sometimes the last event is a fragment and client fails JSON parse.
support_elaine: thanks. Two quick asks: 1) can you attach the raw bytes of one failed session (or the last 1kB) — partial is fine; 2) any intermediaries between client and our edge (LB, Cloudflare, on-prem proxy)?
sarah_cust: attached snippet (sanitized) below — you can see it cuts off in the middle of a JSON object:
```
data: {"id":"r-9a7c2f","object":"chat.completion.chunk","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"{\"items\":[{\"id\":\"a1\",\"text\":\"hello\"},{\"id\":\"a2\",\"text\":\"wo\"}}","index":0}]
```
support_elaine: that looks like a mid-chunk cutoff. @ingrid_eng can you weigh in — could be an upstream connection reset or proxy idle-close while model was still generating.
ingrid_eng: likely causes: upstream connection reset, HTTP proxy trimming last chunk, or client-side read timeout. Quick checks: 1) look at our request logs for r-9a7c2f to see final backend status (200 vs 499/504). 2) check tcp_retransmits / connection close events in our LB logs. I pulled the request and saw the edge logged a 200 but the connection had FIN from the remote IP ~2s before final flush.
netops_tom: from network side — many customer proxies use a 60s idle timeout. SSE with long model think time can appear idle if no events are emitted for >60s, then proxy closes. Our streaming runtime usually streams token fragments frequently, but structured-mode might buffer until larger chunks are available. If buffer interval > proxy timeout you get mid-object cutoff.
support_elaine: that fits. Actionable suggestions for customer: - try enabling periodic heartbeats/comments in SSE (send ":keepalive\n\n" every 15s) or set smaller flush_interval on client to force chunk emission - if using a proxy, increase its idle timeout or whitelist the endpoint - as a fallback, call with "stream": false to get final JSON synchronously
sarah_cust: do you have a minimal repro I can drop in to show them? I can ask infra to bump timeouts if needed.
ingrid_eng: quick repro (node fetch streaming) — client sends and prints raw chunks so infra can see the gap: 
```
const res = await fetch(url, {method:'POST', headers, body: JSON.stringify(payload)});
const reader = res.body.getReader();
while(true){ const {value, done} = await reader.read(); if(done) break; process.stdout.write(new TextDecoder().decode(value)); }
```
If you run this behind the customer's proxy you can show the last chunk gap. For workaround we recommend adding periodic SSE comments from the server side or have client set a lower buffer/flush size.
support_elaine: also added note: if the truncated JSON contains an opening brace without a closing brace, client can try a small retry: call the non-streaming endpoint (stream=false) using same conversation id to get canonical JSON. That avoids double billing? remind: inform customer they'll be billed for both calls — advise compare tokens.
sarah_cust: thanks. I'll send customer the repro snippet + ask infra to raise their idle timeout to 90s. I'll also offer the non-streaming fallback for now.
devops_bot: logged: TICKET-4568 created for tracing r-9a7c2f and evaluating buffer/flush defaults on structured streaming. Assignees: ingrid_eng, netops_tom.
support_elaine: good plan. Follow-up: ingrid, can we add a small server-side heartbeat comment before starting long model decode (>30s) and update docs with guidance for proxies?
ingrid_eng: yes — I'll prototype a 10s comment heartbeat on the streaming runtime and add a config flag to enable for structured-output models. Will post patch link in this thread when ready.
sarah_cust: appreciated, please cc me when ticket updates. I'll close on my side once infra confirms timeout bump. :thumbsup:
